threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say "Can I get a flat white?" instead of just ordering a coffee. It’s a dead giveaway.
Last night on the 196, a guy was serenading the bus with a ukulele. Totally off-key, but everyone joined in on the chorus. Weirdly lovely vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw my neighbor juggling in the street while the local Döner shop set up for a spontaneous block party. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you stumble upon a 24-hour outdoor gym that doubles as a graffiti gallery—weights and art, all under the stars.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to bring a sweater to Dolores Park, even on sunny days. Microclimates are real, folks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy in the Tenderloin turn a broken Muni bus into a dance stage—full crowd around him, no one caring about the wait. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all we eat is tapas. But locals actually grab a bocadillo from the corner bar and skip the fancy dining for a quick bite.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newcomers by their lingering confusion at the metro maps—caught between lines, staring like it’s a riddle.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to Dalston Junction and not just call it the 'Dalston' station like the locals do.
Caught a night bus home from the Elephant, and a bloke was serenading us with 90s R&B. Only in Bermondsey, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a man making a coffee from an old bike under the overpass, it hit me—this is home. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a Döner while waiting for an evening U-Bahn, with street musicians serenading the chaos. It's the perfect blend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re from here if they can name all the taco trucks on 24th without thinking. The newcomers just hit up the trendy spots.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy using the Muni rail as his personal stage, belting out 80s ballads. Crowd clapped, a moment of joy amid the usual chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the best paella is found in Sitges. Meanwhile, the locals know it's just a cheap plate of rice in Gràcia that hits the spot.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a menu in English at local cafés, completely missing the vibe of the Catalan chatter around them.
